title: GM trucks and SUVs: howl, whine, shudder or grinding in 4HI / Auto 4WD, transfer case fluid change
summary: GM bulletin 19-NA-136: a noise or shudder in 4HI or Auto mode (often in parking lots) that goes away in 2HI can come from normal transfer case break-in wear contaminating the fluid. Confirm on a road test, then change the transfer case fluid.

specs.name: Transfer case RPOs
specs.value: NP0, NQ6, NQ7, NQF, NQG, NQH

specs.name: Fluid (US)
specs.value: 88865601 (19421425 in Canada); capacity per service information

specs.name: Labor
specs.value: 0.3 hr diagnostic test and drive; 0.5 hr fluid drain and fill

steps.text: Customer may report howling, whining/whirring, shudder/vibration or grinding in parking-lot maneuvers in AUTO, or at speed in 4HI or AUTO, that goes away in 2HI.
Road test 1: in AUTO, do low-speed parking-lot maneuvers and listen.
Road test 2: in 4HI, accelerate moderately from a stop and listen for growl, howl, whine or whir.
Road test 3: at about 55 mph (89 km/h), switch between 4HI and 2HI and listen for the same noise.
Once the noise is confirmed as the transfer case, replace the transfer case fluid per service information.

body:
GM's cause statement: normal transfer case break-in and wear can create excess contaminants in the fluid.

The bulletin's model-year table doesn't extract cleanly from the PDF, so the year ranges here are the outer bounds it lists (Silverado back to 2014, Escalade from 2015, through 2025). Confirm the transfer case RPO.
